The #133 lifecycle-record projection is a read-only, optional extension of the same composable status slot, not another lifecycle resolver. It displays only `awaiting-author`, `blocked`, and handoff state for an Issue or PR explicitly addressed by an operator act with a platform-attested repository and subject identity. A PR key includes its head; an Issue key has an explicit null head. Absent an addressed target the projection is silent: no current Issue/PR identity or workflow phase is inferred, no merge/decision mode is re-resolved, and no label alone asserts a lifecycle state or authority. Proposed and Active remain distinct; neither a missing label nor an unavailable read establishes Active. The #276 handed-over `.github/workflows/gitjig-lifecycle.mjs` engine owns the record and terminal admission. Its existing `awaiting-author` population inspector and the read-only, terminal-aware `blocked` and handoff inspectors owed by this contract must inspect a pagination-complete, platform-fetched comment population with attested carrying-comment identity. For the latter two markers, which carry no record-side producer or terminal-side clearer field, the carrying User's platform identity and current permission must pass #276's existing same-repository `authorizedResolver` predicate (`WRITE`, `MAINTAIN`, or `ADMIN`); a Bot requires independent first-party-producer proof or is not projected. Every marker and terminal is checked: missing, malformed, duplicate, ambiguous, stale-head, untrusted-author or contradictory populations result in silence, never a guessed current state. This display never writes, clears, authorizes, or blocks an act. It cannot substitute for the transition service or the governing lifecycle record (§2.2).

The projection passes a two-second read bound at its own platform call site, without changing a shared reader's default for any other caller. It computes only on an explicitly addressed act or on-demand request, never polls, and caches only a successful computation for five minutes under repository/subject/head (including the Issue's null head). Timeout, API error, unavailable Pi/UI, and invalid population are unavailable observational state: no TTL stamp, no status call without UI, no blocked act, and no model-visible record body. Status refresh cannot leak one subject's state into another's; the existing active-dispatch/latest-terminal class and #131 dispatch/publish act rendering remain unchanged. Lifecycle projection and #263's later retained-trace inspection are separate operator-only surfaces; neither widens §4.9's model-visible return nor copies raw traces into model context.
